key_insight: A hybrid silicon nanocone-plus-nanohole architecture reduces front reflection and boosts internal light trapping, enabling much higher absorption in thin-film solar cells.
engineering_relevance: This design offers a practical optical-management strategy to raise thin-film silicon PV efficiency while maintaining strong performance under elevated operating temperatures.
method: Front-surface silicon nanocones create a graded refractive-index transition to suppress reflection.
Embedded air-filled nanoholes enhance multiple scattering and internal reflection within the absorber.
FDTD simulations were coupled with electrical and opto-electro-thermal device modeling to optimize geometry and operating conditions.
evidence_signal: Optimized simulations report 34.64 mA cm-2 Jsc, 0.82 V Voc, 86.27% fill factor, and 24.42% efficiency, plus 95.21% efficiency retention at up to 45°C.
watch_item: The reported gains are simulation-based, so fabrication tolerance, nanostructure uniformity, and real-world scalability may affect measured performance.
paper_title: Hybrid Nanocone-Nanohole Light Trapping for High-Efficiency Thin-Film Silicon Solar Cells
